notes: Correct and complete, but it adds duplicate helpers on both Dispenser and Token and leaves the redundant wasQuoted check; tests are extensive.

Correct and comprehensive, but adds redundant Dispenser wrapper helpers with bounds checks and leaves the redundant wasQuoted check; tests are extensive, covering snippets, the no-brace site and the adapt case.
Complete fix with Token helpers and thin Dispenser wrappers; tests include an unclosed-block error case.
Correct and complete apart from HasSuffix; it uses two helper layers (Token plus Dispenser), and its tests include an unclosed-block error case.
Code fix is complete, but it adds an unrelated '.empryo' entry to .gitignore (a tooling leftover); tests are minimal table entries.
Core fix is correct and near-complete, but it adds an unrelated `.empryo` entry to .gitignore, and its tests are parse-table only.
Inline Quoted() checks fix the main paths but miss ArgErr and the anonymous-block check, and it includes an unrelated .gitignore change.
Inline `!Quoted()` checks are repeated everywhere, ArgErr and the anonymous-block check are missed, and an unrelated .gitignore change was left in.
Complete and clean; tests cover dispenser behavior, parser table cases and an integration file with both brace types.
Clean Token helpers applied at nearly every reference site (only the address HasSuffix check is missed), with good dispenser, parse-table and adapt tests.

Updates every structural brace check through Token helpers, but leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(); tests are thorough, including the unclosed-block error case and an adapt integration test.
Near-reference fix but keeps a now-redundant `wasQuoted == 0` check in directive(); its tests are strong, including a check that a quoted `}` cannot close a real block.
Complete and clean, essentially equivalent to the reference; good dispenser and table tests plus an adapt integration test.
Clean near-reference fix with dispenser, parse-table and adapt tests; it misses only the HasSuffix site.
Fixes the reported case but skips the ArgErr, addresses() and the doImport anonymous-block check, so quoted braces are still treated as structural in those paths.

Fixes the main block-parsing paths with clean Token helpers, but leaves the address `{` check, the anonymous-block check in import and ArgErr untouched, so quoted braces are still treated as structural there.
Complete fix using Dispenser helper methods, though doImport duplicates the condition inline; tests are only a few table entries.
Correct via Dispenser helpers, but checks are inline in the doImport switch, HasSuffix is missed, and tests are only a few parse-table rows.
Complete fix with a single stringly-typed isBrace helper; adds a live-server integration test that is heavier than needed.
A single `isBrace(string)` helper is applied consistently and the fix is correct; the added integration test spins up a live server, which is heavier than needed.
Complete, including the HasSuffix address check, but mixes Dispenser helpers with repeated inline Quoted() checks; tests span parser, snippet and httpcaddyfile adapt.

Covers every site in the reference, including the address HasSuffix check; it mixes inline `!Quoted()` checks with Dispenser helpers that carry redundant bounds checks, and its tests are thorough (dispenser, parse segments, snippet import, adapter).
Complete, clean replacement of all brace checks with unquoted-aware helpers and the redundant check removed; solid dispenser and parser tests.
Clean near-reference fix with Token helpers; dispenser and segment-level parse tests are good but include no negative case.

Leaves openCurlyBrace/closeCurlyBrace and the anonymous-block check unchanged, so an unclosed block ending in a quoted '}' (e.g. ':8080 {\n respond "}"') is silently accepted; the text="" switch trick is hacky.

Leaves closeCurlyBrace/openCurlyBrace unquoted-unaware, so a site block left unclosed after `respond "}"` now parses silently; it also skips the anonymous-block check and uses a hacky `text = ""` switch.
Complete, clean fix; parser tests check segment contents and that an unclosed block still errors.
Clean near-reference fix; segment-level parse tests cover nesting and the unclosed-block case.
Complete, clean helper-based fix; strong tests covering backticks, snippets and multi-block parsing, plus an integration file.
Clean near-reference fix with thorough tests covering backticks, snippets, multi-block parsing and an adapt fixture.

The most reference-like fix: it also moves the quoted '{}' handling out of the special branch, and its tests cover snippets and unbalanced-brace errors; using isBrace("{}") is a slight naming stretch.

Matches the reference, including the quoted `{}` condition change in directive() (only HasSuffix is missed); several positive tests only check for no error, but there are good negative unbalanced-brace tests.
Same over-broad parent override, and its unit test explicitly asserts that a child's import of a different instance is dropped, cementing the behaviour the reference treats as wrong.
Partial fix; its unit test codifies dropping the child's overridden["y"] import when the parent only imports ["x"], contrary to the intended instance-level override.
Same over-broad parent override; its unit test asserts that the child's b["y"] import is discarded because the parent imported b["x"].
Partial fix with a string-keyed owner map; its unit test explicitly asserts that a child's b["y"] import is dropped when the parent only imports b["x"], which locks in the wrong semantics.
Has the same resource-level ownership gap, plus an unrelated .gitignore change; it does copy the module path properly.
Same partial fix, plus a junk .gitignore change; only a basic plan test.
Has the same resource-level ownership gap, plus an unrelated .gitignore edit and a duplicated, contradictory doc comment.
Same partial ConfigResource-level fix, plus an unrelated .gitignore entry and a stale, contradictory doc comment left above the new one.
Same resource-level ownership gap; the double append does not actually prevent mutating cfg.Path's backing array; tests are thorough.
Partial fix with an awkward double-append copy and a string-keyed map; the unit test is decent but only covers same-instance override.
Fixes the same-module for_each case, but a parent import of one instance drops all of a child module's imports for that resource, and other instances are silently lost; good unit and plan tests.
Partial fix with a unit fixture and a plan test; cross-module override still applies to the whole resource rather than per instance.
Same resource-level ownership approach with the same nested-module over-dropping; the test covers both for_each and count with reversed declaration order.
Partial fix that leaves the cross-module instance override wrong; its plan test usefully covers count and reversed block order.
Fixes the reported case, but the parent/child override is applied per config resource rather than per instance, which fails the instance-level override tests; it adds a simple two-instance plan test.
Clean but partial fix; the plan test also runs Validate, but cross-module instance-level override is not handled.

Uses the same resource-level ownership claim as most candidates, so a child's imports of other instances are dropped when the parent imports any instance; nice slice-capacity fix and a solid three-instance plan test.
Partial ConfigResource-level fix; the plan test checks each instance but not for extra changes.
Resource-level ownership has the same nested-module gap, and the needless switch to a pointer-to-slice accumulator is less idiomatic than the existing pattern.
Partial ConfigResource-level fix that needlessly switches to a pointer-to-slice accumulator; has only a basic plan test.
Same approach, keyed by an ad-hoc string map instead of addrs.Map, with the same nested-module over-dropping; the plan test does not check the action.
Partial ConfigResource-level fix with a string-keyed map and an aliasing-safe append; tests cover same-module multi-blocks and single-instance parent override.

Adds the reference's instance-level knownImports guard and passes all hidden tests, but its extra config-level dedup ignores module instance keys, so module["a"].res and module["b"].res imports still collapse silently.

Adds the reference's instance-level dedup in expandResourceImports (passes all hidden tests), but its extra static dedup keys on ConfigResource plus resource key and ignores module instance keys, so root blocks for module.x["a"].r and module.x["b"].r still collapse silently.
Same approach and gap; the unit test explicitly expects a child's different-instance import to be silently dropped.
Partial fix; its unit test explicitly expects the child's x["j"] import to be dropped because the parent imports x["k"], baking in the bug.
Fixes the same-module case only; a parent block for one instance still suppresses a child's blocks for other instances; it adds a basic plan test.

Returning a slice fixes the reported same-module for_each case, but parent/child override still works per ConfigResource, so a child's blocks for other instances are silently dropped whenever the parent imports any instance (fails 2/3 hidden tests).
Resource-level ownership fixes the reported bug but fails the instance-level parent/child override cases; it has decent unit and plan tests.

Same ConfigResource-level owner approach: fixes the issue scenario but keeps silent drops across modules, unlike the reference's instance-level override; adds a reasonable unit fixture plus a plan test.
Clean resource-level ownership fix for the reported case that still drops a child's other-instance imports when the parent imports one; it adds a basic plan test.
Clean but partial ConfigResource-level fix with only a basic plan test.
Uses a slug map keyed by section path with prefix lookups, which correctly handles intermediate non-section dirs and DisablePathToLower; it also updates the relevant docs.
Builds a map from section base path to slug and replaces dir segments by prefix, respecting DisablePathToLower; good multilingual test, plus a reasonable but unrequested docs tweak.
A path-keyed slug map applied via prefix matching in CreateTargetPaths is correct, handles unnormalized paths, and fits the existing code well.
Passes a path-to-slug map in the descriptor and applies it by prefix in CreateTargetPaths, skipping when URL or permalink is set; solid and focused.
The prefix-map logic is correct, but the patch leaves a debugging artifact (an empty dbg_test.go) and an unrelated .gitignore change.
Core prefix-map logic is correct, but the patch ships debugging leftovers: an empty dbg_test.go and an unrelated .gitignore entry.
Works for the common cases, but a slugged section whose path skips a non-section dir loses that intermediate segment, and it adds an unrelated .gitignore entry.
Works for common cases and for pages in non-section subdirs, but replaces a whole multi-segment relative section path with the slug and includes an unrelated .gitignore change.
Deliberately skips slugs for pages not directly inside their section, leaving wrong URLs for pages in non-section subdirectories (fails a hidden test).

Deliberately skips slug application for pages not directly in their section, so descendants in subdirectories keep the old path (fails a hidden test); it also collapses intermediate dirs between sections.
Applies depth-keyed slugs to both the section base and the container dir via two override fields; correct, if slightly redundant.
Depth-keyed slugs are applied to both section base and container dir via two override fields; correct, with a slightly redundant API surface.
Hijacks ExpandedPermalink and joins the section chain directly with BaseName, dropping non-section subdirectories of pages (fails a hidden test).
Abuses ExpandedPermalink and joins only section names plus basename, dropping non-section intermediate directories (fails a hidden test) and replacing multi-segment relative section paths wholesale.
Passes, but it overloads ExpandedPermalink, which changes ugly/permalink semantics, and uses path.Base per section, so intermediate non-section dirs are dropped whenever any ancestor has a slug.
Passes tests, but hijacks ExpandedPermalink to carry slug paths, which conflates it with the permalinks feature, and uses path.Base for non-slugged sections, dropping intermediate dirs.
Depth-indexed slug replacement that skips home and standalone pages, with relevant doc updates and a good multilingual test.
Correct depth-based replacement with standalone/home guards; adds docs edits, and the test is adequate but lacks title context and deeper edge cases.
Concise depth-based Dir using cmp.Or, with relevant doc updates and thorough tests covering ugly URLs and term links from pages.
Depth-based replacement over the current section chain with clean cmp.Or fallback; thorough tests (deep nesting, uglyURLs, terms via GetTerms) plus extra docs edits.
Rebuilds the path from path.Base of each section, so it drops non-section intermediate dirs and page subdirectories (fails a hidden test); it also needlessly changes BaseName logic.
Rebuilds the path from ancestor base names only, losing non-section intermediate directories for pages (fails a hidden test), and makes an unneeded BaseName change for branches.

Collects branch slugs by path depth and swaps the matching segments in both the section base and the container dir; this handles non-section subdirectories, though the slice-indexed descriptor field is slightly awkward.
Depth-indexed slug slice applied in CreateTargetPaths works for sections, terms and descendants; sound but slightly fiddly leading-slash handling.
Closely mirrors the reference: it walks section rel-paths replacing only the last element, appends the page's extra container dirs, and tests the non-section subdir case.
Walks the section chain and replaces only the last segment of each relative section path, closely mirroring the reference; the test explicitly covers a page in a non-section subdirectory.
Clean depth-based segment replacement wired through a Dir override; the test is monolingual but covers section, nested, taxonomy and term behaviour.
Replaces dir segments by ancestor path depth, so intermediate non-section dirs are preserved; the test is single-language only and does not cover the multilingual scenario from the issue.
A compact depth-keyed slug map builds a Dir override for pages and branches, with a solid multilingual test covering nested sections, taxonomy and term.
Compact depth-keyed slug replacement that handles nested sections and non-section dirs; test covers multilingual sections, taxonomy and term, and checks the English pages stay unaffected.
Correct depth-based replacement over the current-section chain, with strong tests including ugly URLs and terms without content files.
Correct depth-based approach using paths.FieldsSlash; tests cover uglyURLs and a taxonomy slug applied to terms without content files.
Cohesive applyOnceFlag plus executor.ApplyOnce with a help example and thorough integration, archive and derivation-stability unit tests; it shares the gap around lower-layer shortcut overrides.

Adds a dedicated flag set to run, archive and cloud run and applies ApplyOnce after consolidation; tests cover run and archive end to end, but a CLI-specific error now lives in lib/executor, and env-layer shortcuts and execution-segment flags are not handled.
Fail-fast getOnce and a clean ApplyOnce beside the shortcut derivation, with strong table-driven flag tests, derivation stability, unrelated-option preservation and an archive check via a stdout tar.
Solid implementation with comprehensive tests, including discarded script shortcuts, -i, archive metadata and preservation of unrelated options; the --once logic lives in a public lib package.

Works and keeps raw exec null-ness through a new unexported BaseConfig getter, but the logic is split awkwardly across cmd and executor, it adds unrelated .gitignore junk (.empryo), uses a clumsy hand-rolled test helper, and misses lower-layer shortcuts wiping scenarios.

Works, but adds a hacky unexported method to BaseConfig to read the raw exec (losing exec in the fallback path), includes an unrelated .gitignore change, and has weak tests with a reinvented indexEq helper.

A reasonable ApplyOnce with sorted scenario names in the error, but it always sets exec explicitly via an odd temporary BaseConfig, adds unrelated .gitignore junk, and has only unit tests with no end-to-end run or archive coverage.
The transform works, but exec is always written explicitly (even "default"), an unrelated .empryo entry is added to .gitignore, and only unit tests are included.

Clean separate flag set wired into run/archive/cloud and a well-documented executor.ApplyOnce applied after consolidation, with thorough integration and archive round-trip tests; it does not handle env/config-layer shortcuts that wipe scenarios before consolidation.
Correct transform plus a nice archive round-trip test; checking the flag and applying the transform are combined in one helper, and the CLI message sits in lib/executor.

Clean once.go flag helpers plus executor.ApplyOnce, registered for run/archive/cloud, with good integration tests (tags, env, setup/teardown, conflicts, archive) and unit tests including empty scenarios.
Clean split between flag handling in cmd and the transform in executor, with good tests that use JSON output for tags; the archive test hardcodes a /test path.

With no scenarios it defers to shortcut derivation via vus/iterations=1, which conflicts on an empty scenarios map; isOnceEnabled oddly returns true alongside an error and exec is always set explicitly, though the tests are strong.

Keeps the logic in the cmd package and has very thorough unit, integration and archive tests; with no scenarios it relies on 1/1 shortcuts rather than an explicit scenario, which is equivalent but less uniform.
Clean once.go with its own flag set registered for run/archive/cloud run and good unit and integration tests, though it has no archive test.
Well-contained cmd-package implementation with table-driven flag tests and run tests, but no archive coverage.
Tidy DeriveOnceScenario that clones the env/tags maps and is applied post-consolidation, with comprehensive integration, archive and validate-based unit tests.
Correct transform that clones env and tags and keeps exec unset when it is the default; good run and archive tests, with the CLI error placed in lib/executor.
Self-contained cmd-package implementation close in spirit to the reference, with fail-fast validation and very strong tests (full struct equality, exit codes, archive metadata).

Keeps everything in internal/cmd like the reference, with clean helpers and an exit-coded sentinel error, plus excellent unit, run (including tag) and archive tests; only the lower-layer shortcut edge case is missing.
Clean executor.ApplyOnce with an exported sentinel error and the flag in optionFlagSet, with good unit tests including default-exec handling and end-to-end run/archive tests.
Clean post-consolidation transform that keeps an unset exec unset, with good run and archive tests; it pulls cobra into options.go and exports a CLI-flavoured error from lib/executor.

Solid DeriveOnceScenario next to the shortcut derivation, with the flag registered on all needed commands; tests cover run, multiple scenarios, conflict and archive metadata but are a bit lighter on tags.
Sound implementation with a comparable sentinel error and decent tests, though the archive test does brittle substring matching on JSON.
Functional implementation, but it commits a stray debugging artifact file (internal/cmd/tests/stdout) and its integration test relies on fragile Drain()[0] indexing.
The implementation is fine and stays in cmd, but it commits a stray internal/cmd/tests/stdout debugging artifact, and its test indexes Drain()[0] without a length check.
Reasonable implementation in config.go that always sets exec explicitly; tests are added to existing files with decent unit coverage but no archive or cloud verification.
Compact implementation in config.go that works, but exec is always set explicitly and there is no archive test.
Validates the flag early before CLI parsing and implements DeriveOnceScenario cleanly; tests verify exec, env, tags, the executor type via k6/execution, conflicts and archive contents.

Registers the flag set on run, archive and cloud and applies DeriveOnceScenario after consolidation; good integration tests that verify the executor type at runtime, but it misses lower-layer shortcut dropping and segment conflicts.
Correct ApplyOnce in executor and a flag helper oddly placed in config.go; good unit tests (unrelated options kept, empty scenarios, derivation) plus run and archive integration tests.
Correct transform with good integration and archive tests; it imports cobra into config.go and places the CLI logic in lib/executor.

Traps in hugo_template.go executeWithState, which is good placement. Keeps HasReturn, so output is discarded and an unreached return yields nil. No template-boundary trap, no try passthrough, and the transform error is no longer wrapped with the template name.

Core early return and the legacy argument wrapping work, but the transform-error wrapping is lost, a partial whose return is never reached yields nil, and template-boundary and try handling are missing.

Workable: adds an ExecuteWithReturn API, wraps legacy multi-arg returns and passes through `try`. Keeps HasReturn, so an unreached return gives nil instead of output. Bare return in define/template ends the whole outer template.
Works for basic early return with try and legacy wrapping, but keeps HasReturn so an unreached return yields nil, adds a parallel ExecuteWithReturn API, and has no template-boundary trap.

HasValue semantics match the reference (bare return keeps partial output), plus try passthrough and legacy wrapping, and the package suite passes. No template-boundary trap, no value/pipeline errors, an unrelated .gitignore change, and somewhat messy duplicated tests.

HasValue semantics match the reference (a bare return keeps output) and try and legacy forms are handled, but a return inside a `template` call ends the whole template, there is no pipeline check, and it adds a stray .gitignore entry.
Wrap logic is reasonable, including method calls, and `try` is handled. Keeps HasReturn nil/discard semantics, has no template-boundary trap, and leaves an unrelated .gitignore `.empryo` entry.
Thoughtful legacy wrapping and try pass-through, but no template-boundary trap, an unreached return yields nil, it adds a stray .gitignore entry, and the tests contain unused fixtures.

Closest to the reference: walkTemplateOld rename plus fork-script update, executeWithState trap in hugo_template.go, HasValue so a bare partial return keeps rendered output, try passthrough, and legacy wrapping. Gaps: no error for value-return outside partials, no last-in-pipeline check, and the 13600 regression test was rewritten to pass.

Mirrors the reference's fork-friendly walkTemplate rename and script update, with HasValue semantics, try pass-through, and legacy wrapping; it lacks the pipeline-position check and the value-outside-partial error, and traps value returns at template boundaries.

Cleverly avoids touching the fork by relying on ExecError wrapping. As a result `try` swallows the sentinel. It moves return to the templates namespace, keeps HasReturn nil/discard semantics, and has no template-boundary handling.
Avoids touching the fork by unwinding through ordinary wrapped errors, but this means `try` swallows a return and there is no template-boundary trap; an unreached return yields nil.

Trap placement in executeWithState is good. Breaks legacy `return add . 42` because there is no arg wrapping. No try passthrough or template-boundary trap, and bare return yields an arbitrary empty template.HTML.
Clean sentinel and top-level trap, but it drops `return add . 42` support (breaking an existing test), leaves the 13600 test failing, and has no template-boundary or try handling.

Has a basic sentinel and trap, but drops legacy `return add . 42` support, does not let `try` pass the sentinel through, misplaces the newErrorWithCause doc comment, and its own tests contradict its behavior (asserts `! SKIPPED` and unescaped `<nil>`).
Minimal sentinel, but it breaks `return add . 42`, silently accepts extra args, attaches newErrorWithCause's doc comment to the new type, and leaves the 13600 test failing.

Template-boundary trap and executeWithState trap work. It deletes walkTemplate from the forked exec.go without updating the fork script, which is a maintenance hazard. No try passthrough, bare return gives nil, and return moves namespaces.

Functionally reasonable, with a template-boundary trap and legacy wrapping, but it deletes walkTemplate from exec.go without updating the fork script, so re-forking would break the build; no try handling.

Covers the most edge cases (non-partial value error, last-in-pipeline check, HasValue output semantics, try, template trap). It drops legacy `return add . 42` support and edits an existing hugolib test to hide that regression; it also errors on value-returns inside defined templates in partials.

Closest semantics (pipeline check, value-outside-partial error, try, template boundary, bare return keeps output), but it breaks `{{ return add . 42 }}` and hides this by editing the existing test, and it errors on value returns from sub-templates inside partials.

Clean and focused, with legacy wrapping and try passthrough, and an unreached return yields output. Bare return in a partial yields nil, and a bare return inside define/template terminates the whole outer template.
Clean implementation with try pass-through, legacy wrapping, and fall-through output, but no template-boundary trap and a bare return yields nil rather than the output so far.

Traps return at template invocation, passes through `try`, and wraps legacy args using a proper Copy so the tree is preserved. Bare return in a partial yields nil rather than rendered output, and walkTemplate/errRecover are edited in place in the forked exec.go.
Template-boundary trap, try pass-through, and legacy wrapping are present, but it changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature, edits exec.go directly, and a bare return yields nil.
Template-boundary trap (in-place exec.go edit), legacy wrapping, and a three-value execute API are reasonable. No try passthrough, and bare return in a partial gives nil instead of output.
Template-boundary trap and legacy wrapping work, but there is no try pass-through and no argument-count validation, it changes the store API signature, and a bare return yields nil.

Adds a method to the forked parse package to wrap args, and passes through `try`. Bare return in a partial yields nil, there is no template-boundary trap, and applyTransformations keeps a dead bool return.
Reasonable approach with try pass-through, legacy wrapping via a new parse helper, and fall-through output, but no template-boundary trap and a bare return yields nil.

Lets the sentinel through `try` and validates arg count. Has no argument wrapping, so existing `{{ return add . 42 }}` templates break. Keeps HasReturn discard/nil semantics and edits errRecover in exec.go in place.
Has try pass-through, but no legacy `return add . 42` support (an existing test regresses), no template-boundary trap, and a partial whose return is never reached yields nil.
Traps return at template boundaries, though via an in-place exec.go edit, and wraps legacy args (partials only). Keeps HasReturn nil/discard semantics and lacks try passthrough.

Sentinel return works and a return inside a `template` call ends only that template, but a bare return yields nil instead of the output so far, there is no try pass-through, and exec.go is edited directly instead of through the fork mechanism.
Clean, small fix plus a useful durations_test for evaluating a unary-plus wrapper; StartPos uses the literal rather than the paren, and Pretty and the lost parse-time checks are not addressed.
Minimal, reference-like wrapping, plus an evaluation test for unary-plus DurationExpr; parse-time `foo[(0)]` validation is lost and Pretty is unchanged.
Sound wrap helper plus a constantDuration positive check; Pretty is not updated and no test covers the new positive-check behaviour.
Clean `parenDurationExpr` and `constantDuration` helpers keep the parens and the positive-duration check; no test covers the new `foo[(0)]` validation and Pretty is not updated.
Fix works but carries a '.empryo' .gitignore leak, precomputes values that require an unrelated subquery printer reorder, and adds a stray blank line in tests; Pretty is not handled.
Wraps the literal correctly and keeps parse-time validation and constant Range/Offset values, but adds an unrelated `.gitignore` entry, flips the subquery Step print order, and does not fix Pretty.
The core fix and positive check are fine, but it leaks an unrelated '.empryo' .gitignore entry and puts tests in a separate ad-hoc file instead of the existing printer tests.
Correct wrapping with added constant validation and a good round-trip stability test, but leaves an unrelated `.gitignore` entry and does not fix Pretty.
Fixes round-trip and Pretty, but also precomputes Range/Step/Offset alongside the expressions, which forces an unrelated reorder of subquery step printing, so scope grows noticeably.
Thorough: wraps literals, keeps validation, fills Range/Offset from constants, fixes Pretty, and has strong AST and error tests, at the cost of extra refactoring and a printer Step-order flip.

Takes a different route: a public Wrapped field on NumberLiteral, an addOffset signature change, durationExprOf in several grammar rules and a subquery printer reorder; it works but is invasive and changes the API.

Takes a divergent hybrid approach: a new public `NumberLiteral.Wrapped` field plus wrapper DurationExprs, special cases in the grammar, an `addOffset` signature change, and a printer change; it works but is invasive and convoluted.
Reference-like fix including Pretty, with a partial div/mod-zero preservation; it does not restore the positive check and the zero-check change is untested.
Reference-like wrapping plus the Pretty fix and a partial divide-by-zero helper (misses `-(0)`); positive-duration parse validation is lost and tests only cover round-trips.
Works but uses awkward double negation inside the NumberLiteral branch, adds an unrequested experimental-flag check, uses literal positions instead of paren positions, and does not touch Pretty.
Works, but negates then un-negates the literal and adds an unrequested experimental-flag gate inside `applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr`; no validation or Pretty handling.

Wraps a bare literal in a unary-plus DurationExpr and keeps the parse-time positive-duration check via literalDurationSeconds; it leaves Pretty unchanged and includes a regenerated header-line diff as noise.
Correct wrapping with preserved `<= 0` validation and a `foo[(0)]` test, but it rewrites the generated-file header (would fail check-generated-parser) and passes the op item as the 'open paren'.
Thorough: generic wrapping and preserved positive and div/mod-zero checks with strong tests, but refactors applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr to take a *posrange.Pos and skips Pretty.

Restructures `applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr` around a reference-like `wrapDurationExpr`, preserves validation and divide-by-zero checks, and has excellent tests; the signature refactor is broader than needed and Pretty is untouched.
Works with a special-cased positive check that covers only (N), not -(N); has a redundant range check and the inner StartPos uses the operator position; Pretty is not updated.
Fixes the round-trip but its special-cased validation only handles a wrapped plus literal, so `foo[-(5)]` slips through; no Pretty fix.
Correct, with accurate paren positions via a new parenPos parameter; it adds churn to the applyUnaryOp signature and the generated header line, and handles neither Pretty nor the parse-time checks.
Accurate paren positions via a new `parenPos` param, but drops parse-time `foo[(0)]` validation, skips Pretty, and changes the goyacc header in the generated file.

Correct, with a generic positive check, but builds the node inline in the grammar, has inconsistent StartPos handling between + and -, includes a redundant range check, and has no test for the new check.
Works and keeps positive-duration validation, but the wrapped-literal path juggles StartPos and redundant range checks, and there are no tests for the validation.
Close to the reference including the Pretty unary-plus fix, plus a generic positive check; has a minor redundant range check and no test for the positive-check change.
Clean helper-based fix with preserved validation and a Pretty fix matching the reference; tests cover round-trips but not the validation path.
Most complete: wraps any non-DurationExpr like the reference, updates Pretty, preserves positive and div/mod-zero parse-time checks, and tests them; only a small StartPos imprecision.
Wraps literals, keeps both positive-duration and division/modulo-by-zero parse checks via `constantDuration`, fixes Pretty, and tests both error paths.
Minimal fix close to the reference with accurate paren start/end positions and good round-trip tests, but Pretty is not updated and the parse-time positive/zero checks lost for (N) are not restored.
Closely mirrors the reference wrapping, including Start/End positions, with focused tests; parse-time `foo[(0)]` validation is lost and Pretty is not fixed.
